Rendering `Compose.circle(0, 0.5, 0.1)` 
followed by `polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)])`
using various
`Compose` `context` parameters.

```{julia}
using Gadfly, Compose

set_default_plot_size(3inch, 2inch)

composition = 
  compose(context(),
      (context(),
        fill(nothing), stroke("grey"), 
        (context(), 
          Compose.circle(0, 0.5, 0.1), 
          text(0.01, 0.76, "Produced by\ncontext()\nat ()", hleft, vtop),
          polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]))),
      (context(),(context(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
          (context(),
            Compose.circle(0, 0.5, 0.1),  
            text(0.12, 0.65, "Produced by\ncontext(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)\nat (0, 0.5)"), 
            fill("gray")), 
          (context(),
            polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]),
            fill("bisque"), stroke("grey"))),),
      (context(),
        (context(0.2, 0.0, 1, 1),
          (context(),
            Compose.circle(0, 0.5, 0.1),  
            text(0.11, 0.5, "Produced by\ncontext(0.2, 0.0, 1, 1)\nat (0, 0.5)"),
            fill("gray")), 
          (context(),
            polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]),
            fill("cornsilk"), stroke("grey")),)),
)
```

We now study the interaction of `UnitBox` settings in `annotations` of `Gadfly` plots.
There are small shifts in the `UnitBox` transformations, perhaps due to axis
space!

```{julia}
annot = compose(context(), 
  (context(), polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.5), stroke("grey")),
  (context(), text(0.05,0.1,"raw polygon")))
plot(f, 0, 1, Guide.annotation(annot))
```

```{julia}
annot = compose(context(units=UnitBox(0, 0, 2, 2)), 
  (context(), polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.5), stroke("grey")),
  (context(), text(0.05,0.1,"halved polygon", hleft, vtop)))
plot(f, 0, 1, Guide.annotation(annot))
```

```{julia}
annot = compose(context(units=UnitBox(0, -1, 2, 2)), 
  (context(), polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.5), stroke("grey")),
  (context(), text(0.05,0.2,"halved polygon\nwith vertical shift", hleft, vtop)))
plot(f, 0, 1, Guide.annotation(annot))
```


Consider on the other hand
```{julia}
annot = compose(context(), 
  (context(), polygon([(0,0), (0,0.5), (0.5,0.5), (0.5,0)]), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.5), stroke("grey")),
  (context(), text(0.05,0.2,"halved polygon\nwith vertical shift", hleft, vtop)))
plot(f, 0, 1, Guide.annotation(annot))
```

Also try working with `context`: the same problem arises.

```{julia}
annot = compose(context(0w, 0h, 1w, 1h), 
  (context(), polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.5), stroke("grey")),
  (context(), text(0.05,0.2,"no shift in context", hleft, vtop)))
plot(f, 0, 1, Guide.annotation(annot))
```

```{julia}
annot = compose(context(0w, -0.5h, 1w, 1h), 
  (context(), polygon([(0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0)]), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.5), stroke("grey")),
  (context(), text(0.05,0.2,"vertical shift in context", hleft, vtop)))
plot(f, 0, 1, Guide.annotation(annot))
```
